title: HIV+ Tumor Molecular Characterization Project - Lung Cancer
summary:
People living with HIV have substantially elevated lung cancer incidence and worse outcomes, and are close to absent from the cohorts that define lung cancer genomics. This is the smallest cohort we have made a showcase page for, and we included it because size is not the only thing that determines whether a dataset is worth knowing about.
All 39 cases carry whole genome sequencing, 38 RNA sequencing and 37 microRNA. 26 patients are recorded as Black or African American. Pathologic stage is recorded for 62% and prior treatment for 92%, both unusually good for a cohort of this size.
one_liner: 39 lung cancers from an HIV-enriched cohort, two thirds Black or African American, with whole genome sequencing on every case and clinical staging on 62% - very small, and addressing a population that appears in almost no lung cancer genomics.

useful_for.question: Does lung cancer arising in people living with HIV differ genomically from lung cancer in the general population?
useful_for.rationale: Whole genome sequencing on all 39 cases, contrastable with the large TCGA lung cohorts in the same repository under the same harmonization. Whole genome rather than exome allows mutational signature and structural analysis.
useful_for.statistical_note: 39 cases supports descriptive comparison of signature burden and recurrent alterations only. Any difference must be large to be detectable, and the comparison cohorts differ in sequencing era and platform.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Can this cohort serve as a validation set for HIV-associated cancer hypotheses?
useful_for.rationale: Alongside the cervical and lymphoma cohorts in the same program, it allows a hypothesis about HIV-associated tumor biology to be tested across three tumor types collected under a common protocol.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: What is the survival experience of this population?
useful_for.rationale: Vital status is informative for 89.7% of cases, with follow-up derivable for 36 of 39 and extending to 104 months despite a short median of 6.4.
useful_for.statistical_note: 35 cases with informative vital status and a 6.4-month median follow-up gives very wide confidence intervals. Report them and avoid median survival estimates.

limitations.statement: 39 cases is the smallest cohort with a showcase page here. Nearly every analysis is underpowered, and no subgroup analysis is viable.
limitations.mitigation: Use for descriptive characterization or as a validation set for an externally derived hypothesis. Do not attempt discovery.

analysis_examples.title: Treatment response, after checking the response field is real
analysis_examples.question: Is performance status associated with response to chemoradiation, and which agents were actually given?
analysis_examples.problem: Disease-status codes and true response categories are easy to mix into one misleading outcome.
analysis_examples.lesson: Validate the response field, collapse repeated records, and state what the observational result cannot prove.
analysis_examples.figure: Two panels: a bar chart of how many cases carry each response label against how many carry none, and box plots of ECOG performance status for responders against progressors.
inputs: Open GDC clinical records for CGCI-HTMCP-CC
outputs: Separation of genuine response categories from disease-status codes
Per-case responder/progressor labels under a stated rule
Mann-Whitney comparison of ECOG between response groups
A two-panel chart of response composition and ECOG by response group
steps: Facet the two response-bearing fields and classify their values
Collapse one-to-many treatment records to one label per case
Compare performance status between response groups
Tabulate the therapeutic agents actually recorded
